text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.35% today to $134.19, capping a four-day climb that's added roughly $7 to the stock. The driver is straightforward: oil prices surged on geopolitical risk. World oil hit $125.44 per barrel today amid reports of Iranian tanker attacks on shipping and escalating U.S. military threats toward Iran—including talk of "massive bombing" operations and Treasury sanctions on Iranian oil tankers. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly lift the value of reserves and production.

The move also reflects tightening global supply. A hurricane threat to U.S. Gulf production combined with disruption to Iranian exports (a major global supplier) creates genuine scarcity concerns that push prices higher across the board—benefiting any large-scale oil producer regardless of where it operates.
